ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, officers, shareholders and individuals with significant control against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian autonomous sanctions issued under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and FINTRAC's published guidance on domestic and foreign politically exposed persons. Beneficial ownership must be verified and recorded in the CBCA register of individuals with significant control (ss. 21.1–21.4); reporting entities under the PCMLTFA must maintain an audited compliance program, risk assessment, and client identification records. Corporate service providers must also observe FATF Recommendation 24 and Canada's beneficial ownership transparency directives.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada – Online Filing Centre (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada), using the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system for federal name searches and reservations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A federal corporate name must be in English, French, or a combined bilingual form (CBCA s. 10). The name must contain a distinctive element, an optional descriptive element, and a mandatory legal element such as Limited, Limitée, Incorporated, Incorporated, Corporation, Corp., Inc., or Ltée (CBCA s. 10(1)). Transliterations from non-Latin scripts must be submitted in an official transliteration acceptable to the Director of Corporations Canada, and the name must not be confusing with any existing federal, provincial, or territorial entry in the NUANS database or with a protected trademark under the Trademarks Act.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Banking, Trust, Trustee, Loan, Insurance, Assurance – require prior approval under federal financial-services legislation
Canadian – permitted only where the business clearly indicates Canadian ownership/control or with ministerial consent
Royal, Empire, Imperial – imply governmental patronage and require the consent of the Governor in Council or the Director
University, College, Institute, Academy – require consent of the competent education authority
Police, Ambulance, Undertaker – require consent of relevant public authorities
Olympic, Olympia – protected under the Olympic and Paralympic Marks Act
Terms suggesting the corporation is a public body, an agency of the Crown, or a municipality
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a NUANS refusal or an objection to a confusing name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Director of Corporations Canada under CBCA s. 12.1, including supporting evidence of distinguishability such as a disclaimer, an additional distinctive element, or the written consent of the holder of the confusing name or trademark. If the Director upholds the refusal, the applicant may require the Director to refer the matter to the Federal Court for judicial review under CBCA s. 12(3). Reconsideration submissions should be filed promptly within 30 days of the notice of decision to avoid expiry of the underlying NUANS report, although the CBCA does not prescribe a fixed statutory appeal window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally acceptable for a Low_Risk_Standard consultancy (ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541611) provided that the CBCA registered office requirements are satisfied: a physical street address in Canada where corporate records and the register of individuals with significant control are accessible during business hours, and where process may be served. Pure mail-forwarding operations without a Canadian street address do not meet CBCA s. 19. In practice, service-based virtual offices in Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal and Calgary are accepted for non-regulated consultancies.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – approximately 1–3% probability per annum for this non-licensed, low-risk consultancy sector. Unannounced physical inspections are generally reserved for regulated financial, money-services and high-risk sectors; however, FINTRAC compliance examinations and CRA audits may request access to books, records and the UBO register at the registered office address without substantial advance notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-44), sections 5 (incorporation), 6 (articles), 9 (name), 16 (registered office), 106-128 (directors and officers), and 213 (corporate records)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, Industry Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) filed electronically via the Corporations Canada online filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under the CBCA; shares may be issued for any lawful consideration, and no escrow account is mandated
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. That the articles of incorporation as filed by the incorporator are hereby adopted, and the corporation is authorized to carry on business as a foreign market entry consultancy. 2. That the corporation subscribes for and accepts all issued common shares, with consideration approved by the board. 3. step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online portal via Industry Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed corporate name through the online NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system. Review pre-approved name options, ensure compliance with CBCA name regulations, and obtain the NUANS report for attachment to the incorporation filing. The name must not be confusingly similar to an existing trademark or corporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or reserved by another entity, file a new NUANS request with an alternative name or submit a rebuttal/consent letter from the confusingly similar holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and File Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form 4001 (Articles of Incorporation) electronically through the Corporations Canada online system. Include the NUANS report, specify registered office address, define share structure, list initial directors, and declare any restrictions on business activities. Pay the applicable registration fee via credit card or pre-authorized debit.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director for each director
Office address consent form if not yet executed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the flagged fields (e.g., deficient NUANS report, incomplete director information) within the prescribed response period through the online resubmission portal; re-submit with amended data and pay any revised fee if applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After successful review, Corporations Canada issues a Certificate of Incorporation bearing the federal corporation number. Download the certified copy from the online portal. The certificate is conclusive proof of incorporation. Retain it for banking, licensing, and tax registration purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certificate is delayed, contact Corporations Canada support or initiate an expedited service request; verify whether a compliance review was triggered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (physically or by teleconference). Adopt by-laws, approve share issuance to initial subscribers, appoint officers, confirm the registered office, choose the fiscal year end, and pass the pro-forma first board resolution. Maintain minutes in the corporate records book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If organizational documents are defective, adopt corrective resolutions ratifying actions; re-execute any insufficiently authorized agreements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Registration for Tax and Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and provincial/territorial registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a federal Business Number (BN) and open applicable CRA accounts (e.g., corporate income tax, GST/HST if annual revenues exceed $30,000, payroll if employees are hired). If operating in a province, complete extra-provincial registration or obtain a provincial incorporation license as required; apply for a municipal business license.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA account application is delayed, verify the federal BN; provide additional documentation (such as certified articles) and follow up with the CRA Business Registry. For provincial issues, resubmit the application to the provincial registry with correct supporting evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 7020 (management consultancy) is an office-based intellectual service and does not require industrial licensing under federal or provincial frameworks
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial manufacturing or operational permit required; the entity must hold a general municipal business license and, where applicable, a provincial registration certificate for consulting services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the proposed activity is purely office-based with no physical construction, manufacturing process, or discharge of regulated emissions
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for normal office operations; if leased office renovation occurs, applicable municipal waste disposal, low-VOC finishing material, and fire safety standards must be met

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and occupancy permit required for the leased office premises under the applicable municipal building code and local fire department regulations; workplace occupational health and safety clearance follows the applicable provincial occupational health and safety legislation (e.g., Ontario Occupational Health and Safety Act)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA-ARC), 4th Floor, 555 Mackenzie Avenue, Ottawa ON; statutory tax filing and registration portal: 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/business-taxes.html); GST/HST registration portal: 'Business Registration Online' (BRO) at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-business/business-number-registration-online.html; customs and export reporting portal: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA)/Canadian Export Reporting System.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a federal business corporation incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) and held by non-residents: (1) file Articles of Incorporation with Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development (ISED) — no minimum capital requirement; (2) upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, the CRA automatically issues the 9-digit Business Number (BN), which is the statutory TIN, together with the RC corporate income tax program account; (3) before commencing taxable commercial activity, open the GST/HST RT program account via BRO or Form RC1, and for non-resident applicants via Form RC4601 ('Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts'); (4) where the corporation will have Canadian-resident employees, open the RP payroll account; where goods are embedded in consultancy deliverables, open the RM customs/export account; (5) the combined 15-character program account identifier (e.g., BN '123456789' + 'RT0001') must appear on GST/HST returns, invoices, and customs documents. Registration is mandatory once taxable supplies exceed the C$30,000 small-supplier threshold, and the BN/RT account application must be filed within 30 days after ceasing to be a small supplier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: CA_CORP is a resident corporation under subsection 250(4) ITA by virtue of federal incorporation and is taxed as a separate Part I taxpayer on worldwide income (federal general corporate rate 15.0%; 9.0% small business rate only where the corporation is a Canadian-controlled private corporation — unavailable if non-resident-controlled); no pass-through, transparent, or S-corporation-type treatment exists for CBCA corporations; the same entity-level taxation applies provincially/territorially (e.g., Ontario 10.0% general corporate rate); non-resident-owned CBCA corporations remain resident Canadian corporations and therefore are not taxed on a purely territorial basis.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style 'check-the-box' election; classification follows legal form. Available elections relevant to this cross-border consultancy: (i) subsection 256(2.1) ITA election for a non-resident corporation to be deemed resident for the loss-utilization and associated-corporation rules; (ii) subsection 216(1) ITA election for a non-resident to file a Part I return on Canadian-source property/rental income instead of Part XIII withholding; (iii) the Part XIV branch-tax 'investment allowance' election computed under Income Tax Regulations 808-810 to reduce the 25% branch tax base of a non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada; (iv) GST/HST nil-consideration election under section 156 ETA (Form RC4129) for supplies between closely related corporations; (v) GST/HST joint group-registration election among closely related residents under Part IX Excise Tax Act. Hybrid mismatch consequences are non-elective and are governed by ITA sections 18.4 and 18.5 (BEPS Action 2).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST — federal Goods and Services Tax and provincial Harmonized Sales Tax, imposed under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA) and administered by the CRA; Quebec administers a parallel QST under a tax-collection agreement with the CRA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 (CAD) — GST/HST registration is mandatory for a person carrying on a commercial activity in Canada whose total taxable supplies made in Canada exceed C$30,000 either in a single calendar quarter or in the last four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold, subsections 240(1) and 240(1.1) ETA); zero-rated export supplies are excluded from the threshold calculation; a non-resident supplying services into Canada is subject to the same threshold, and once exceeded the RT account application must be filed within 30 days after ceasing to be a small supplier.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, government API tax-stamping, or continuous-controls e-invoicing mandate is currently in force in Canada at the federal level. GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding C$1.5 million must file returns electronically (GST/HST NETFILE / My Business Account), and electronic remittance is mandatory where monthly payroll withholdings average more than C$50,000. CRA administers the voluntary 'Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing' PEPPOL-based interoperability framework, but participation is optional; regardless, subsection 286(1) ETA requires all registrants to retain books, contracts, invoices, and transaction logs for six years, and CRA may demand contemporaneous zero-rating substantiation on audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The overseas market-entry consulting services supplied by CA_CORP to non-resident clients are zero-rated under section 23 of Schedule VI to the ETA where: (1) the recipient is a non-resident of Canada with a foreign business address and economic substance; (2) the supply is not in respect of real property situated in Canada; (3) the supply is not in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at any time; and (4) the service is not rendered to a non-resident who is present in Canada at the time and for whose benefit the service is performed with a connection to Canada. Any tangible goods physically exported as part of a deliverable (e.g., demonstration kits, printed reports) qualify for zero-rating under section 7 of Schedule VI and must be supported by a CBSA export declaration. The registered supplier must retain contemporaneous proof of non-resident status, the place of performance, and actual receipt of consideration; mischaracterized domestic services (where the foreign client directs or benefits from the consultancy within Canada) will be reclassified as taxable at 5% GST plus applicable provincial HST/PST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System / authorized carrier cargo declaration evidencing departure of any tangible deliverable from Canada
Bill of Lading or air waybill issued by a common carrier evidencing shipment of physical media, prototypes, or printed reports to the overseas client
Inward Remittance Certificate — SWIFT MT103, Wise B2B transaction receipt, or bank credit advice evidencing receipt of consideration from the non-resident payer
Written market-entry advisory contract identifying the non-resident recipient, offshore subject matter, scope of work, and place of performance
Itemized commercial invoice bearing the notation 'Zero-rated export supply — section 23, Schedule VI, Excise Tax Act (Canada)'
Foreign client address and non-resident status attestation confirming the consulting output is received and used outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a zero-rated export claim within four years of the GST/HST filing date (subsection 298(1) ETA) and within four years for corporate income tax (subsection 152(3.1) ITA); where misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, willful default, or fraud is established, the reassessment window is unlimited. Penalties for fraudulent export zero-rating include: (i) a false-statement penalty of the greater of C$250 and 25% of the net tax assessed under subsection 280(1) ETA; (ii) a gross-negligence income tax penalty of 50% of the understated Part I tax under subsection 163(2) ITA; (iii) criminal prosecution under section 327 ETA and section 239 ITA — fines up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment; (iv) daily compounded arrears interest and recovery of over-credited input tax credits; and (v) application of the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (section 245 ITA) where the zero-rating claim lacks substantive economic reality. A transaction file failing the 180-day repatriation substantiation benchmark of this dossier will be treated by CRA as presenting elevated audit risk and presumed insufficiency of documentary evidence for the zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration exists, and exchange control functions are subsumed by Finance Canada, OSFI, and FINTRAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada accepts Article VIII obligations; the Canadian dollar is fully convertible on current and capital account. Profit remittance does not require exchange-control permission, but Part XIII withholding tax (typically 25% statutory, up to 5% or 25% reduced under the Canada-U.S./double tax treaties) and transfer-pricing rules are the material hurdles for overseas market-entry consultancies repatriating earnings. Investment Canada Act review may impose notification or net-benefit conditions when a non-resident acquires control of a Canadian business, but it does not block currency conversion or lawful dividend flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender period, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no exchange-control filing for the retention of export foreign currency. Export receipts may be held in foreign-denominated bank accounts; only PCMLTFA-based threshold reporting applies to international electronic funds transfers in excess of CAD 10,000, which is discharged by the financial institution.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability as supplemental payment rail. Offshore digital EMIs and specialized providers such as Wise B2B are lawfully available for low-value cross-border disbursements, but cannot hold corporate deposits as a Canadian bank; Canadian-licensed deposit-taking institutions are required to act as the primary treasury layer. Fintech EMIs must be integrated only for small ticket consultancy payments and fast FX settlements, with the main operating and escrow accounts at a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank to satisfy CBCA oversight, FINTRAC reporting, and bank comfort requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandatory physical appearance exists under Canadian AML/KYC law; banks apply risk-based CDD and may permit remote video verification, notarized identities, and trusted-introducer sign-off. In practice, a foreign-director federal corporation opening a business operating account will be required to attend a recorded video interview, provide notarized passports and proof of address, and in some cases complete an in-person appointment at a Canadian branch. Under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), at least 25% of directors must be resident Canadians for a federal corporation, so the director pool must evidence Canadian residency; foreign directors can satisfy identity requirements remotely through a Canadian counsel or notary, but the banking relationship manager will require a clear, documented KYC consent process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder injection structured as share capital while operational expenses are paid in multiple overseas currencies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate organizational chart, CBCA certificate and articles, board resolution authorizing share subscription, share certificates, source-of-funds documentation from the remitting bank, audited or reviewed financial statements, and a written treasury plan explaining the commercial purpose of each cross-border movement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) opacity, especially if a trust, unregulated holding vehicle, or nominee shareholder is in the ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed corporate registry UBO register filed under CBCA, identification for every individual holding 25% or more, trust deed or settlement deed if applicable, sworn beneficial ownership declarations, and a Canadian legal opinion confirming that no undisclosed indirect owner exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status or adverse media on directors, shareholders, or high-level employees
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Point-in-time commercial PEP/media screening reports, government-issued notarized identity documents, professional reference letters from a regulated Canadian or foreign financial institution, biographical resume, and documented legal source of wealth (tax returns, inheritance documents, property sale contracts, or publicly audited corporate payouts).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substantial incoming wire from a low-transparency jurisdiction or an exchanger/high-risk jurisdiction that does not align with cash-flow nature of a consultancy
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty due diligence questionnaire, client engagement agreement, deliverables schedule with client-approved invoices, remittance breakdown showing payment for specific advisory services, exporter/importer details on the SWIFT message, and where necessary a Canadian counsel memorandum on the legitimacy of the funding source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large volume of outbound disbursements for sub-contracting or licensing fees with mismatched invoice references
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed sub-consultancy or license agreements, invoices cross-referenced to payment dates and SWIFT MT103 reference fields, proof of registered GST/HST account or evidence that supply is zero-rated for non-resident clients, timesheets or milestone certifications, and periodic reconciliation statements submitted to the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections for a Canadian federal consultancy are executed by International Central Securities no; the practical route is a SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wire to the beneficiary's Tier-1 Canadian bank account using the bank's BIC, institution number, branch transit, and account number. Field 70 (Remittance Information) should explicitly cite 'Share capital contribution pursuant to board resolution dated [date]' or 'Intercompany shareholder loan' so the wiring-bank narrative matches the corporate treasury record. Canada does not maintain a statutory purpose-code or forex approval regime for incoming capital; the bank must simply complete FINTRAC's large-international-funds-transfer report where the amount exceeds CAD 10,000. The corporate must pre-position the share subscription agreement, director resolutions, and CBCA share register for presentation during any hold-funds review. If the inbound transfer is from a non-resident parent or private shareholder, treat it as capital for CBCA solvency purposes only if issued shares with consideration; otherwise, document an intercompany loan with arm's-length interest and written treasury support.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and consultancy disbursements should clear via SWIFT MT103 for beneficiary banks outside Canada, particularly for licensing, sub-consultancy, and overseas market-entry registrations. Documentary trade counterparties may enforce Commercial Letters of Credit issued under UCP600 where escrow payments or milestone deliveries require bank-verified documentation. For domestic Canadian-dollar flows, Payments Canada's Lynx high-value system handles same-day settlement, while the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) processes batched EFTs and pre-authorized debits for non-urgent vendor payments. FX conversion is executed at the ordering bank in the same working day before the MT103, with the corporate treasury maintaining a separate CAD operating account and a multi-currency settlement account to minimize conversion slippage. Where only small disbursements are needed and supplier contracts allow, Wise B2B can be used as an approved payment rail; otherwise all material treasury-grade payments must route from the primary bank through SWIFT.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards for CAD against USD, EUR, CNY, GBP, and JPY
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps for smoothing intercompany cash-flow timing
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the referencing currency lacks deliverable settlement or statutory support
OTC FX options (call/put structures) for asymmetric protection on large licensing or M&A-related one-off payments
Exchange-traded FX futures via recognized Canadian and U.S. exchanges for short-dated hedge rollovers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return (Form 4006) including Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each annual anniversary of the date of incorporation; online filing is the standard filing route.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after the 60-day window may attract a prescribed late fee; failure to file for two consecutive years can trigger a notice from the Director and administrative dissolution under CBCA s.212. A dissolved corporation loses legal capacity and must be restored at prescribed fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (corporate income tax declaration, including financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the end of the corporation's fiscal/taxation year; tax balance payment is generally due two months after year-end, with a three-month window for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under ITA s.162(1) is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, with increased rates for repeat failures; daily interest applies to unpaid amounts; continued non-filing may trigger arbitrary assessment and prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The CBCA does not impose a size/revenue audit threshold for private federal corporations. An auditor must be appointed at each annual meeting unless all shareholders, including non-voting shareholders, unanimously consent to dispense with an auditor each year. A reporting issuer must always appoint an auditor, and lenders may contractually require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises; private federal corporations may prepare financial statements using IFRS or Canadian ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) as Canadian GAAP. CRA record-retention minimum is ordinarily six years from the tax year-end; a seven-year retention policy is common for corporate books.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Federal CBCA corporations must maintain a register of individuals with significant control (ISC Register) and update it within 15 days of any change in significant control, including share transfers resulting in an ISC becoming or ceasing to be an ISC. Effective January 22, 2024, prescribed ISC information must be included in the annual return filed with Corporations Canada; there is no separate annual share-transfer confirmation filing. The registered shareholder list and ISC Register must be reviewed annually and minutes/board resolutions should confirm continued accuracy.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200-700 per year for a provincial registered-office address and mail-forwarding service; full corporate compliance agent services (annual meeting minutes, annual return reminders, ISC register maintenance) typically total USD 400-1,000 per year.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000-15,000 for a full CBCA audit of a small non-reporting federal corporation; USD 1,500-4,000 for a review engagement where the audit is validly waived.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal Part I general corporate rate (net of 10% federal abatement and 13% general rate reduction on a 38% base rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CCPC Small Business Deduction reducing the federal rate from 28% to 9% on the first CAD $500,000 of active business income; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) ITC 33% refundable (small CCPC); accelerated CCA classes for eligible equipment; investment tax credits available for qualifying expenditures; provincial credits may apply
